predecessors.name: Haiti
predecessors.text: the north of the Haitian state of Dessalines, taken by Christophe after the assassination of 17 October 1806

successors.name: Haiti
successors.text: the northern kingdom, reunited with the south by President Boyer after Christophe's death on 8 October 1820

rulers.name: Henri Christophe (President, then King Henri I)

ledger.x: 17 October 1806: Christophe founds the State of Haiti in the north.
1807: the war with Pétion's south begins.
1810: a peace treaty splits the country in two.
28 March 1811: Christophe is proclaimed King Henri I.
October 1820: Christophe takes his own life and Boyer reunites Haiti.

wars.name: War between Christophe's north and Pétion's south
wars.outcome: Stalemate: two states side by side until Christophe's death in 1820; Pétion died on 29 March 1818 and Boyer succeeded him.

certainty.note: The line between the north and Pétion's south is not described on any page opened; it is a de facto front, not a surveyed or treaty line.
